findings.reason: the graph-only re-judge is one flag (stored-text-only, no SSH) on the existing reset+worker owner, so §3's five new drivers fork scoping and status ownership that already exists and will drift.
findings.text: §3 adds "one re-judge driver beside each pipeline's claim functions" and §7 runs it "per facility and pipeline ... scoped and bounded", rebuilding the status reset plus facility and path-prefix scoping that `reset_to_status(spec, facility, path_prefixes=...)` already owns; the census of existing owners the plan should extend instead is `SIGNAL_RESET_SPECS` (reset.py:163), `PATH_RESET_SPECS` (:264), `WIKI_RESET_SPECS` (:320), `CODE_RESET_SPECS` (:378), `DOCUMENT_RESET_SPECS` (:433), dispatched through `DOMAIN_RESET_SPECS` (:453) and already wired to a `--reset-to` CLI at imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py:218, paths.py:244, wiki.py:355, code.py:197, documents.py:133

findings.reason: extracting one `discovery/base/` judge-and-apply driver parameterised by each pipeline's questions/state/apply collapses five drivers to one and is where the complexity belongs.
findings.text: the judgment behaviour the plan would add (per-row state build, `acall_decisions`, validation, cost booking, apply-or-leave, claim/release) is a deep module the code pipeline already implements inline in imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:270 and imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:76; §3 spreads that same behaviour across five per-pipeline drivers, so the plan grows surface five-fold over one shared driver rather than adding depth

findings.reason: without the justification the honest change is to extend the existing driver with a source-of-text flag, not to add a second path per pipeline.
findings.text: each proposed re-judge driver forwards to `call_decisions` with a pipeline's own question template and per-row state, the shape already proven by `build_triage_questions`/`build_triage_state`/`apply_triage_results` (imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:76,107,475); the plan justifies neither why the existing pipeline worker cannot be extended with a graph-only mode nor why the code pipeline's driver is not made shared, so the wrappers are a parallel copy

findings.reason: naming the reset owner and the true response-model homes changes which files §3–§6 declare as the files they modify.
findings.text: the plan's search covers `call_decisions` and the §25 code pipeline for the gate forms, but misses the re-processing owner above, and its §2 census mislocates the response models it would replace — `TriageBatch` and `ScoreBatch` live in imas_codex/discovery/paths/models.py:126,214 (not `paths/scorer.py`/`paths/parallel.py`) and `ImageScoreBatch` in imas_codex/discovery/wiki/models.py:470 (not `base/image.py`) — so the prior-art map is incomplete at the two files the design would actually edit

findings.reason: extending the existing reset/worker owner (see duplicate_owner) removes the added definitions entirely, and the section must account for the surface it adds.
findings.text: every supplied figure is zero (public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0), yet §3 introduces new public re-judge driver definitions without stating any it retires or merges, and §9 introduces "a seat named for the rerank" beside the existing seats in imas_codex/settings.py:181-185 without naming a seat it retires; no section states why nothing can be retired

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §3 spreads one behaviour (build state from stored fields, ask `call_decisions`, apply the answers, book the cost) across five per-pipeline re-judge drivers instead of one shared driver in `discovery/base/`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3/§7 re-implement facility- and prefix-scoped status re-processing that `imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py` already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds five re-judge drivers and §9 adds a rerank seat without naming, in its own text, what each retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the mechanism it extends for the judgment calls (`call_decisions` in `imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py` and the §25 code pipeline), but it never searches the machinery that already re-processes stored rows: `imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py` and the `--reset-to` CLI in `imas_codex/cli/discover/`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the five re-judge drivers add no behaviour the existing pipeline worker plus the reset path lacks other than a graph-only flag, and the plan does not say why the pipeline cannot take that flag.
